title: Where does dough rise well?
question: Does dough rise better somewhere warm or somewhere cold?
steps: Drag the dough bowl to the oven or into the fridge.
Once the bowl is down the time runs by itself. While it runs the buttons at the bottom left are locked.
Use the buttons at the bottom left to put the yeast in or leave it out.
observe: Yeast is a living thing too small to see. It eats the sugar in the dough and breathes out a gas, so bubbles form in the dough and it rises. Where it is warm the yeast works hard and the dough rises fast; in the cold fridge it rises very slowly. Without yeast it never rises, however long it waits.

terms.name: Yeast
terms.description: A living thing too small to see that goes into bread dough. It eats sugar and breathes out a gas.

terms.name: Fermentation
terms.description: When tiny living things like yeast eat their food and turn it into other things. Bread rising is fermentation.

terms.name: Gas bubbles
terms.description: Little pockets of the yeast's gas caught in the dough. They are the holes you see when you cut bread.

law.title: Yeast makes dough rise
law.description: Living yeast eats the sugar in the dough and makes a gas. The gas is trapped in the dough, so it rises. Yeast is busy when warm and almost rests when cold, so dough rises much better somewhere warm.

tip: Drag the dough bowl to the oven or the fridge and the time runs by itself. Drag the bowl again and the time stops; put it down and it goes on.

stages.text: Make the dough twice as big by the oven!
stages.say: Somewhere warm the yeast makes lots of gas, so the dough rises.
stages.miss: Put it by the warm oven!

stages.text: Without yeast? Does it rise even somewhere warm?
stages.say: Without yeast there's no friend to make the gas. So it doesn't rise, even when warm.
stages.miss: Watch until the night is over!

stages.text: Make the dough rise up to the piece on the shelf!
stages.say: Dough with yeast kept warm keeps rising. In the cold fridge it only rises a little.
stages.win: It reached the shelf! A piece!

story.keeper: There's only this much flour left. How can the four of us share it? And the dough is flat…

before.text: Bread? Leave it to me! If the dough rises, a little makes a big loaf.

story.clue: There's a piece up on the high shelf! If the dough rises that far it can reach it.
story.map_clue: In the kitchen village, the bakery with the high shelf!

kid.intro: This is the dough lab. The **yeast** we put in dough is a living thing too small to see. It eats the sugar in the dough and breathes out a gas, and the dough rises.
kid.title: Put the dough somewhere warm!
kid.say: Yeast makes a gas and the dough rises. It rises well when warm, and without yeast it stays the same.

note.law: Living yeast makes a gas and the dough rises. The warmer, the better it rises; without yeast it doesn't rise.
note.learn: Dough with yeast doubles by the oven and, left longer, rises up to the shelf. In the same time in the fridge it rises only a little, and without yeast it stays the same through the night. Really, dough takes about an hour to double somewhere warm (about 27 °C) and about 12 hours in the fridge (about 4 °C). The gas that raises it is carbon dioxide.
talk: Why does bread have lots of little holes when you cut it?
On a cold winter day, where would you put dough to rise?
note.formula: volume = start volume × 2^(time ÷ doubling time); doubling time: 27 °C 1 h, 4 °C 12 h
